state.bodyText:
🕌 Salah Widget

A compact prayer-times widget you can embed anywhere that accepts an <iframe> — built for TablissNG new-tab dashboards, but works in Notion, a personal site, or anywhere else.

Static delivery, with saved configuration in browser storage and service requests described below. Configuration comes from the URL; prayer times come from the free Aladhan API. This CP9 integration candidate is not the deployed main version. It adds an admitted star catalogue and physical sky in an optional worker while preserving the prayer widget. See integration, evidence and open gates.

For development, edit src/native/ and the authored real-sky/native-* adapters, then run python tools/build_native.py. Serve with python -m http.server 8000 and open http://localhost:8000/index.html. offline.html embeds sky assets for local file entry; live prayer/weather and fonts still need network access. Root entries and sky bundles are generated; do not hand-edit them.

Live widget: https://theislampill.github.io/salah_widget/ Build your own embed: https://theislampill.github.io/salah_widget/builder.html

Quick start

The easiest path is the builder page — it auto-detects your time zone, can use your browser location, shows a live preview, and gives you a copy-paste snippet.

Or write the iframe yourself:

<iframe
  title="Prayer Times"
  referrerpolicy="no-referrer"
  src="https://theislampill.github.io/salah_widget/#lat=24.4672&lon=39.6142&tz=Asia%2FRiyadh&label=Madinah&method=4&school=0"
  style="width:325px;height:530px;border:0;border-radius:28px;overflow:hidden"
  scrolling="no">
</iframe>


Everything after the # is configuration — change it to your own location.

Using it in TablissNG

TablissNG can't run scripts, but it can embed an iframe. Add an HTML / iframe widget and paste the snippet above (with your own coordinates).

One-line install (optional setup wizard)

The optional installer detects supported browsers and profiles, downloads a TablissNG extension asset and stages a preset for manual import. The Install widget button on the builder copies the normal command for your OS:

# macOS / Linux: run in a terminal with a readable controlling terminal
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theislampill/salah_widget/main/install.sh | bash

# Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe), or supported PowerShell 7 (pwsh.exe)
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theislampill/salah_widget/main/install.ps1 | iex


The Windows response-string command executes the downloaded text in the host where you paste it. Windows PowerShell 5.1 is the declared minimum; the retained PowerShell 7 qualification is version 7.6.6. The commands below use one selected host. Your execution policy still applies; a policy refusal is not installation.

Normal Bash mode requires a readable controlling terminal for every human answer, including when the script arrives through a pipe. No terminal or EOF at the initial target selection refuses before staging. EOF at a later question refuses further progress with manual work pending. Files already staged or retained may remain, and previous clipboard changes or opened pages are not undone; the bundle lifetime rules below still apply. A successfully read empty answer can use the displayed default. Profile discovery is newline-delimited and cannot represent profile paths containing newlines. Spaces, Unicode and literal backslashes remain ordinary path bytes.

If you configured the widget in the builder, Install widget carries its encoded settings through SALAH_WIDGET_HASH into the preset iframe. For a reviewed local-file invocation, keep that environment value, or pass -WidgetHash on Windows, if you want the same configuration.

The wizard downloads and stages files, offers clipboard paths and opens the browser's manual pages. Extension installation and preset import remain manual; it does not silently install extensions or write to browser extension storage. Importing the preset replaces your current TablissNG dashboard with the widget layout. Precise in-widget location also needs the iframe's allow="geolocation"; hosts may strip it, while coarse auto-detect still works.

Review a pinned file first

These examples download the installer at a pinned source commit. Read it, use the optional offline preview, then run normal mode when ready:

curl -fsSL -o ./install.sh "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theislampill/salah_widget/18ff14860ff41c084b1db5f396bb62aa9c22b1be/install.sh"
less ./install.sh
DRY_RUN=1 bash ./install.sh
bash ./install.sh


On Windows, Invoke-WebRequest -OutFile keeps the downloaded file bytes. Review with Get-Content -LiteralPath; do not resave the file through Get-Content/Set-Content or change its encoding. Choose either host below:

Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing -Uri "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theislampill/salah_widget/18ff14860ff41c084b1db5f396bb62aa9c22b1be/install.ps1" -OutFile ".\install.ps1"
Get-Content -LiteralPath ".\install.ps1"
powershell.exe -NoProfile -File ".\install.ps1" -DryRun
powershell.exe -NoProfile -File ".\install.ps1"


For the supported PowerShell 7 host, replace the two powershell.exe calls with pwsh.exe -NoProfile -File ".\install.ps1" -DryRun and pwsh.exe -NoProfile -File ".\install.ps1". Run one host's normal command.

Offline local preview

With reviewed local files, preview performs offline local discovery and prints planned actions:

DRY_RUN=1 bash ./install.sh

powershell.exe -NoProfile -File ".\install.ps1" -DryRun
# Supported PowerShell 7 alternative:
pwsh.exe -NoProfile -File ".\install.ps1" -DryRun


Preview asks no questions or terminal answers. It creates no staging or usable artifacts and makes no writes, extraction, copy, removal, cleanup, clipboard, browser, profile or extension effects. It requests no remote metadata, provider, download or network-availability information. Remote release/version/path and source choices that local discovery cannot settle remain unresolved. Legacy-only or no eligible targets and malformed options are explicit refusals. Preview is neither installation, staged completion nor proof that a remote asset is available.

NO_OPEN=1 bash ./install.sh or a Windows -NoOpen argument applies to normal mode and suppresses opening browser/pages only. Downloads, staging, configured preset work, clipboard offers and manual actions still occur. Choose DRY_RUN=1 or -DryRun for the offline preview boundary.

Bash bundle and cache lifetime

Normal Bash staging creates separate TMPDIR/salah-widget-download.XXXXXXXX scratch and HOME/salah-widget-install.XXXXXXXX retained manual bundles. Keep the unpacked extension directory while that extension is installed. After manual preset import or XPI installation, preset/XPI files may be removed manually if you no longer need them; the wizard does not promise automatic removal.

Completed and explicitly partial retained bundles survive source exit, failure and interruption. Consult the retained path and completion state before manual use. Cleanup removes only unchanged verified scratch, leaving the retained bundle and preexisting user files. Retained files are not a promise of permanent liveness or proof of browser installation.

A valid asset cache hit within one attempt reuses the exact existing path without another asset download. A new invocation creates new verified private scratch; old shared caches and retained manual bundles are not admitted as trusted cache for a new run.

Self-configuring (local) mode

If you don't want to hard-code coordinates — e.g. a generic embed that anyone can drop in — use local mode. Add #local=1 to the URL and the widget will:

try a coarse, permission-free area auto-detect (approximate, IP/timezone-based),
show prayer times for that estimated area,
let the viewer open settings inside the widget (tap/click the header buckle — it morphs into a ⚙ gear on hover/focus; keyboard Enter/Space and touch work too) to correct the location or any setting,
save their choice locally (in their own browser) for next time.
<iframe
  title="Prayer Times"
  src="https://theislampill.github.io/salah_widget/#local=1"
  allow="geolocation"
  style="width:325px;height:530px;border:0;border-radius:28px;overflow:hidden"
  scrolling="no">
</iframe>


A generic #local=1 embed chooses method and units automatically after area detection. A local embed exported by the builder includes the selected method and temperature units as defaults for a viewer with no saved configuration, for example #local=1&method=2&units=f. An existing saved configuration in that viewer’s browser takes priority over those defaults. The generic preset remains #local=1.

The in-widget settings panel supports location (name, latitude, longitude), calculation method, Asr school, 12/24-hour, date format, and temperature units. A location pin beside the location field identifies an estimated area, browser/saved browser position, or manually selected site. Its title reports available accuracy in metres and original fix age; tap it to request a browser position. Type a place name to search (Enter cycles multiple matches; Shift+Enter keeps a custom display name without moving the coordinates). Changes save automatically when you close the panel. If persistence fails, changes apply for this session and Settings retains a warning. The ↺ icon removes only saved widget configuration and then re-detects if removal succeeds; prayer/weather caches and provider-held data are unaffected.

Modes & precedence
Mode	URL	Behaviour
Hardcoded	#lat=…&lon=…	Fixed location baked into the URL. Unchanged, classic behaviour. A saved local config never overrides it.
Local	#local=1	Saved local config → else coarse auto-detect → else in-widget manual setup.
Prefer-local	#preferLocal=1	Like hardcoded, but a saved local config (if any) may override the hash defaults — because the URL explicitly opted in.

Resolution order: explicit hardcoded hash (unless local=1/preferLocal=1) → saved local config → coarse IP/timezone detect → manual setup → safe error state.

Auto-detect, precise location & privacy

Saved configuration uses this browser's storage. Local persistence does not prevent external requests: the table below describes the current recipients, triggers and sent fields. This is a description of source construction and caller controls, not a new transmission trace. Connection IP accompanies external requests. Provider retention or handling is not established by this widget-source description.

Request group	Trigger	Recipient	Sent fields and limits
Approximate area detection	Builder initialization; widget coarse-detection paths, including local/preferLocal resolution and Reset re-detection when the resolver requires it.	GeoJS https://get.geojs.io/v1/ip/geo.json, then https://ipinfo.io/json on failure.	Connection IP; neither URL has typed-query or coordinate parameters. IANA timezone detection uses local Intl. IP-derived area is approximate and is not precise permission or GPS.
Place/postcode search	Builder one-second debounce or Enter; widget Settings Enter. Trimmed queries shorter than 2 make no request.	Nominatim https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/search	q contains the trimmed query; format=jsonv2, addressdetails=1, limit=5. countrycodes is the known home country only for a query containing a digit; alphabetic London has no digit-country bias.
Canadian-style prefix assist	Whitespace removed from a query with a leading letter-digit-letter pattern; in addition to Nominatim.	Zippopotam https://api.zippopotam.us/ca/<FSA>	First 3 matched characters, uppercased: M5V2T6 → /ca/M5V. No complete postcode or widget coordinates are appended. This is a prefix test, not complete-postcode validation; malformed longer queries with that prefix also trigger it.
Builder coordinate reverse lookup	Eligible coordinate edits after 700 ms debounce, or permission-granted builder location acquisition. Stale/non-numeric coordinates and both automatic label/method controls off produce no request.	BigDataCloud https://api.bigdatacloud.net/data/reverse-geocode-client	latitude, longitude, localityLanguage=en, e.g. 51.5/-0.12. This is the builder caller; in-widget browser location does not invoke builder reverse geocoding.
Prayer requests	Eligible date-specific prayer acquisition, subject to existing cache/currentness rules.	Aladhan https://api.aladhan.com/v1/timings/<date>	latitude, longitude, method, school; requested date in the path.
Weather requests	Eligible active current/hourly acquisition, subject to cache, simulation and currentness guards.	Open-Meteo https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast	latitude, longitude, timezone, temperature_unit (celsius/fahrenheit), wind_speed_unit=ms, forecast_days=3, and the current/hourly field selections listed below. These requests do not establish direct local precipitation observation.
Radar evidence requests	Eligible manifest, then returned latest-past frame/tile under existing weather guards.	RainViewer https://api.rainviewer.com/public/weather-maps.json and returned tile host/frame.	Returned host + frame path + /256/<z>/<x>/<y>/2/1_1.png; x/y indices derive from coordinates and disclose a location-derived area. The manifest has no coordinate query. Image alpha is not millimetres or direct local observation.
Font loading	Page stylesheet/font loading, subject to cache/network policy.	Google Fonts stylesheet fonts.googleapis.com and font resources fonts.gstatic.com.	Family/style/weight stylesheet request and returned font-resource URLs; no widget location/search fields in these source URLs. Cache-dependent declarations do not mean every font is fetched on every load.

Open-Meteo's exact selected fields are:

current=temperature_2m,apparent_temperature,relative_humidity_2m,dew_point_2m,wind_speed_10m,wind_direction_10m,wind_gusts_10m,cloud_cover,cloud_cover_low,cloud_cover_mid,cloud_cover_high,visibility,is_day,weather_code,precipitation,rain,showers,snowfall
hourly=temperature_2m,apparent_temperature,relative_humidity_2m,dew_point_2m,cloud_cover,cloud_cover_low,cloud_cover_mid,cloud_cover_high,wind_speed_10m,wind_direction_10m,wind_gusts_10m,precipitation,weather_code,visibility,is_day

Browser location is optional and user-triggered. The location pin requests one browser position after permission. Its reported accuracy may be known in metres or unknown; five decimal places do not measure accuracy. In an iframe, the local snippet includes allow="geolocation", and the embedding parent's Permissions Policy and user grant also apply. Stripping delegation or restricting parent policy can block acquisition; coarse/manual setup remains available.
Acquisition and saving are separate. A browser position retains its original acquisition time and reported accuracy; a saved browser position is a stored target and does not establish current presence. Saving settings does not renew a fix. Missing, malformed, nonpositive or future acquisition timestamps stay unknown; future timestamps have zero skew allowance against Date.now(). Portable URLs describe a configured destination and omit private acquisition history.
Storage outcome is measured. Saved settings use this browser's storage. If writing is unavailable, changes still apply for the current session and Settings shows a retained warning. A partition can be writable and retain settings within that partition. Saving and persistence depend on the host's actual storage permissions and lifetime; blocked writes cause the session-only warning.
Reset scope. Reset removes only the saved widget configuration (salah_widget:config:v1); it does not erase prayer/weather caches or data held by external providers. Successful removal may re-detect the area and issue the coarse request above. Failed removal reports the failure and leaves the existing target usable.
TablissNG conditions. Coarse acquisition depends on permitted provider access; browser position depends on preserved delegation, parent policy and user grant; saving depends on writable host storage and its lifetime. These conditions are not a claim that a particular TablissNG version or partition policy has been qualified.
Configuration (URL hash parameters)
Param	Required	Default	Description
lat	✅	—	Latitude, e.g. 28.93084
lon	✅	—	Longitude, e.g. -82.39122
tz		America/New_York (hint)	Initial IANA zone hint for the bootstrap request date. Admitted provider or selected-cache metadata resolves the location zone; a record must match that zone's current civil day before current timetable paint. Pass a known zone (e.g. Europe/London, / encoded as %2F) as a hint.
label		Prayer Times	Location name shown on the widget. Encode spaces as %20.
method		2 (ISNA)	Calculation method — see table below.
school		0	Asr calculation: 0 = standard, 1 = Hanafi (later Asr).
time		24	Clock format: 24 (15:45) or 12 (3:45 PM).
datefmt		YYYY-MM-DD	Date format as a token string — YYYY/YY year, MMMM/MMM/MM/M month, DD/D day (e.g. DD MMMM YYYY, MMM D, YYYY). The old preset keys iso/us/eu/long still work. Applies to both the Gregorian and Hijri dates.
units		f	Weather temperature: f (°F) or c (°C).
local		—	#local=1 → self-configuring mode: coarse auto-detect + in-widget settings, saved locally. When set, hash lat/lon are ignored in favour of the saved/detected config.
preferLocal		—	#preferLocal=1 → use hash lat/lon as defaults, but let a saved local config override them (opt-in).
lp		0	Light-pollution dial 0–1 — raises the night-sky glow and erases the faintest stars / Milky Way.

Tip: don't know your coordinates? Right-click your location on OpenStreetMap → Show address, or just use the 📍 button on the builder page.

Calculation methods
method	Authority
0	Shia Ithna-Ashari
1	University of Islamic Sciences, Karachi
2	Islamic Society of North America (ISNA)
3	Muslim World League
4	Umm al-Qura University, Makkah
5	Egyptian General Authority of Survey
7	Institute of Geophysics, University of Tehran
8	Gulf Region
9	Kuwait
10	Qatar
11	Majlis Ugama Islam Singapura, Singapore
12	Union des Organisations Islamiques de France
13	Diyanet İşleri Başkanlığı, Turkey
14	Spiritual Administration of Muslims of Russia
15	Moonsighting Committee Worldwide
16	Dubai
Features
Current model weather — Open-Meteo's current model condition and available temperature appear in the header. The condition is an estimate; it is not a direct local observation. Fresh current-model interval amounts can support model rain or snow. A thunder code does not authorize observed lightning. The weather icon has a concise accessible name. Its hover title and accessible description separate current, nearby, approach and forecast information. Live nearby observations and arrival intervals are unavailable. Explicit simulation data is labelled SIM. Unavailable amounts or probabilities are stated as unavailable, and zero remains zero. Unavailable temperature is blank; an admitted zero displays 0° with the existing rounding. Finite negative temperatures are valid in the captured Celsius/Fahrenheit request units. A usable condition can remain when optional measurements are missing. Missing/invalid amounts retain null and a reason, and cannot independently enable wet particles; a genuine zero is a dry model amount. This changes no cache schema and cannot recover whether a historical coerced zero was genuine. In ordinary real time, expired/unavailable current weather shows an em dash and blank temperature when painted, with unsupported weather effects off. Weather cache loading accepts receipt age less than six hours (six hours is a miss), without renewing the separate 15-minute current-use fence or the original receipt. The prayer cache is separate. Client wall-clock errors can affect age checks; stored weather does not guarantee offline availability.
Weather-reactive color theme — the palette shifts with the sky: warm gold under a clear day, deep indigo on a clear night, muted grey when cloudy, cool steel-blue for rain, icy for snow, and charcoal-violet for thunderstorms. Day vs. night is derived from the prayer Sunrise/Sunset times, so it always matches the widget.
Next prayer front and centre. The countdown uses elapsed time to the admitted prayer instant in the location zone, including DST changes; the arc and progress keep their wall-time geometry. The duration rounds to the nearest second, then shows hours and whole minutes at one hour or more, whole minutes at one minute or more, and seconds below one minute.
Progress bar showing how far you are through the current interval.
Location day and time zone — tz is an initial hint. Admitted provider or selected-cache metadata resolves the location zone, and current acceptance uses that zone's civil day at adoption. Without a usable cached zone, bootstrap uses the hint day and may make at most one corrected-day request in the same operation.
Cached prayer data — only an admitted selected current-day record can paint current before refresh. Corrupt cache is a miss; healthy live recovery remains reachable. Valid wrong-day cache may resolve the zone but cannot be called current. Valid current data survives a failed refresh or denied persistence. Existing salah:lat|lon|_cacheTz|method|school bytes remain compatible without scanning, purging or migration; this is not an offline-application guarantee.
Bounded retry — each prayer operation has at most three attempts, with 900/1800 ms backoffs and a 10000 ms deadline for the full asynchronous fetch/body attempt. Bootstrap and corrected-day requests share that budget. Three timeouts total a nominal 32700 ms, plus event-loop scheduling; timers cannot preempt synchronous parsing or a blocked event loop and do not guarantee provider latency. Same-day no-data recovery and failed tomorrow acquisition use a 60-second operation-start cadence on performance.now() hosts, with busy ownership preventing overlap. A valid matching tomorrow suppresses redundant requests; day and generation changes reclassify eligibility. Hidden/offscreen loops pause, so the first resumed eligible opportunity starts one operation without background or catch-up guarantees. Real elapsed eligibility is independent of simTime, timeScale and wall-clock correction. The retained Date.now() fallback is not claimed monotonic.
Weather retry — fetch plus JSON body consumption shares one 10-second application attempt. A radar manifest fetch plus JSON body shares a separate 10-second attempt; once accepted, a new 10-second Image attempt covers dispatch and result consumption. The nominal combined radar application wait is at most 20 seconds while JavaScript is runnable; this is not a hard wall-time recovery guarantee during blocked/suspended execution or scheduling delays. Weather retry is eligible after 60 seconds and radar after 10 minutes from their respective last attempt starts, using the existing client wall clock. An eligible current record plus a retained hourly track can skip weather refetch for less than 15 minutes after the last accepted current receipt. Valid coordinates and free request ownership still matter. The ordinary visible render loop offers approximately 30-second opportunities outside an advancing sweep; eligibility and timeout release are not immediate retry or successful recovery. On performance-clock hosts, the absolute elapsed attempt deadline is checked as well as the timer: a late fetch/body/Image completion is rejected even if suspension delayed timer delivery. The existing Date.now() fallback is a wall clock and is not promised to be monotonic. Timeouts settle the wrapper, release ownership and ignore late results; abort is best effort and detached Image handlers do not prove physical cancellation of every download. No provider-health, offline-service or memory-recovery guarantee is implied.
Passed prayers dim; the upcoming one is highlighted.
Gregorian (CE) date bottom-left and Hijri (AH) date bottom-right, in your chosen datefmt (defaults to ISO YYYY-MM-DD).
Admitted timetable and optional dates — all six events Fajr, Sunrise, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha require valid clocks and matching Gregorian identity. Sunset is optional with Maghrib fallback; supported parenthesized clock suffixes and equal/reordered captured polar schedules remain supported. Rejected records never supply fabricated precise prayer times. Missing or structurally malformed optional Hijri data supplies no usable date. If no usable selected AH value remains, the footer says Hijri date unavailable while the valid timetable remains usable. Hijri structural checks (month 1–12, day 1–30, positive integer year) do not calculate a religious calendar. Name-bearing formats need a usable month name; numeric-only formats do not.
Unavailable countdown — when a required matching next-day record is absent or wrong-date, or its wall time has an invalid, unsupported, ambiguous or gap inverse, the central time is an em dash and the message is Countdown unavailable. A valid current timetable, calendar and arc remain usable; no estimated tomorrow Fajr or invented zero is shown. An admitted matching tomorrow with a unique supported prayer instant restores time/countdown on the next visible dirty frame, including a frozen preview. Unsupported fold disambiguation remains unavailable.

Click or tap either CE or AH date, or Tab to it and press Enter or Space, to open Calendar dates. It shows both complete selected dates, any preview and the current explanation. Scroll and select long values to read their full text. Close or Escape dismisses the view and returns focus to the date that opened it. Reading dates does not apply settings, save data or request another calendar value.

Files
File	Purpose
index.html	The widget itself.
builder.html	Interactive embed-code generator (portable and self-configuring snippets).
config.js	Shared WidgetConfig module (window.SalahConfig) — parse / validate / serialize / load-save local config / coarse auto-detect. Loaded by both index.html and builder.html so config logic can't fork.
install.sh / install.ps1	Optional setup wizard (macOS-Linux / Windows): detects the browser, downloads the TablissNG extension asset, and stages the preset for manual import. No silent installs.
presets/salah-widget.tablissng.json	A ready-made TablissNG dashboard export (this widget in self-configuring mode) that the installer imports.
Deterministic smoke test

The no-build smoke page characterizes the widget with controlled inputs. Copy a complete candidate tree to a disposable directory and use a fresh disposable browser profile or isolated test context. Serve it on an unused loopback origin; do not use your normal widget/Pages origin or clear its storage. For example, replace the directory below with your disposable copy:

python -m http.server 8765 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory 'C:\path\to\disposable-tree'


Open each mode as a separate document:

http://127.0.0.1:8765/tests/smoke.html?fixture=healthy
http://127.0.0.1:8765/tests/smoke.html?fixture=reject
http://127.0.0.1:8765/tests/smoke.html?fixture=hang
http://127.0.0.1:8765/tests/smoke.html?fixture=bootstrap-error

healthy supplies matched prayer responses. reject rejects prayer fetches; hang leaves them pending. Neither negative mode can count an unconsumed response as ready. Their readiness deadline normally produces INCOMPLETE, with FAIL taking precedence if an error is recorded. bootstrap-error deliberately fails before widget parsing and is FAIL. These are separate controlled runs, not an offline skip or successful fallback.

The denominator is 30 named required callbacks, with 141 expected assertions in the current source. PASS requires every callback to finish with exactly its declared assertion count and no failed assertion or other error. The executed count includes cases recorded as executed or failed; pending or missing cases remain missing. A recorded failed assertion or callback, harness or bootstrap error makes the summary FAIL, even when cases are also missing. With no recorded failure, any missing case makes it INCOMPLETE. The pass/fail counters count assertion/error log lines, not completed callbacks; read required.total, required.executed, required.missing and each case in window.__smoke. Late callbacks cannot complete a missing case. The existing limits are 8 seconds for scene readiness, 4 seconds for a required callback and 3 seconds for Moon image decoding.

The wrapper installs a fresh private Map-backed localStorage for each fixture before product parsing; config checks receive separate private or denied stores. No test requires clearing user-origin data. It starts no-argument Date/Date.now() at 2026-09-07T09:30:00.000Z, retains explicit date arguments (controlled cases can advance the private clock), and uses latitude 24.47, longitude 39.61, Madinah, method 4, school 0, timezone Asia/Riyadh and qa=1. Its only admitted Aladhan requests are the four-parameter timings requests for 07-09-2026 and 08-09-2026. Synthetic timings are Fajr 05:00, Sunrise 06:00, Dhuhr 12:00, Asr 15:30, Sunset/Maghrib 18:00 and Isha 19:30. Gregorian and invented Hijri fields are test inputs, not a Hijri conversion claim. The initial 12:30 scene checks actual current Dhuhr, next Asr 15:30 and 180 minutes remaining. Weather uses a fixed Open-Meteo model input and an empty RainViewer index; admitted synthetic weather records exercise their own lane. None is a direct local weather observation.

Readiness binds the unique run, attempt, document, exact scene hash and fetched index.html SHA-256. It also requires actual current-day Response.json() consumption, the matching weather bridge and prayer/render state. An earlier iframe, matching hash alone or stale response is insufficient. Save the final summary, window.__smoke, every attempt's fixture/request/JSON/error ledger, browser/version and file hashes before opening the next mode. The fixture's source digest identifies the fetched index; record config, wrapper and other runtime identities separately.

The wrapper keeps product script bodies unchanged and rejects unknown script/digest/resource anchors. Its current anchors reject the inline Moon startup/refinement layout (moon-initial-code / moon-refinement-code) with Unreviewed widget script anchors; that entry needs a separately reviewed wrapper adaptation before this instrument can qualify it. Retain the failure rather than bypassing the guard. The fixture removes the three known external font links and its policy blocks fonts and external connections. Controlled time, synthetic providers and suppressed fonts cannot certify appearance, readability, normal-live M0 motion, public deployment or every platform. The smoke page's scope notice and separate native/delivery gates still apply.

Credits

Prayer time calculations by the Aladhan API, current-model and hourly forecast weather by Open-Meteo, and unitless mosaic imagery by RainViewer. These browser requests carry the configured location and request context. Settings and caches are stored in the browser when storage is available. RainViewer imagery supplies diagnostics; its alpha values are not rainfall amounts, direct local precipitation or lightning observations.

Preserved V1 compatibility URL

After the preservation PR is merged and Pages deploys, /salah_widget/v1/ serves the frozen pre-overhaul application. The root URL remains the current version. V1's clock, location, prayer timetable, weather and externally hosted fonts remain live. Local settings and caches use V1-specific keys; valid existing root settings are copied once without changing root data.

<iframe
  title="Prayer Times"
  referrerpolicy="no-referrer"
  allow="geolocation"
  src="https://theislampill.github.io/salah_widget/v1/#local=1"
  style="width:330px;height:534px;border:0;border-radius:28px;overflow:hidden"
  scrolling="no">
</iframe>


For the current version, change only src to https://theislampill.github.io/salah_widget/#local=1. The iframe dimensions and internal card layout are unchanged. This compatibility example keeps its 330×534 wrapper around the 325×530 card for both URLs; current-root builder exports and the main embed examples use 325×530 wrappers. See preservation provenance, validation and limitations.

GeoJS https://get.geojs.io/v1/ip/geo.json, then https://ipinfo.io/json on failure.

Place/postcode search
Builder one-second debounce or Enter; widget Settings Enter. Trimmed queries shorter than 2 make no request.
Nominatim https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/search

Canadian-style prefix assist
Whitespace removed from a query with a leading letter-digit-letter pattern; in addition to Nominatim.
Zippopotam https://api.zippopotam.us/ca/<FSA>

First 3 matched characters, uppercased: M5V2T6 → /ca/M5V. No complete postcode or widget coordinates are appended. This is a prefix test, not complete-postcode validation; malformed longer queries with that prefix also trigger it.
Builder coordinate reverse lookup
Eligible coordinate edits after 700 ms debounce, or permission-granted builder location acquisition. Stale/non-numeric coordinates and both automatic label/method controls off produce no request.

latitude, longitude, localityLanguage=en, e.g. 51.5/-0.12. This is the builder caller; in-widget browser location does not invoke builder reverse geocoding.

latitude, longitude, method, school; requested date in the path.
Weather requests
Eligible active current/hourly acquisition, subject to cache, simulation and currentness guards.

latitude, longitude, timezone, temperature_unit (celsius/fahrenheit), wind_speed_unit=ms, forecast_days=3, and the current/hourly field selections listed below. These requests do not establish direct local precipitation observation.

Page stylesheet/font loading, subject to cache/network policy.

Family/style/weight stylesheet request and returned font-resource URLs; no widget location/search fields in these source URLs. Cache-dependent declarations do not mean every font is fetched on every load.

state.bodyText:
salah_widget — AGENTS

How agents (human or AI) should work on this repo. The runtime entry is generated index.html; changes are visual and physics-adjacent, so review is dominated by looking at rendered pixels, not by reading metrics.

CP9 source ownership and qualification

Read docs/real-sky/INTEGRATION.md and the retained post-CP9 DAG before changing this candidate. Edit native UI, prayer/weather, geometry, PBR, Earthshine and embedded lunar textures in src/native/index.html; edit config and builder in src/native/. Integration owners are real-sky/native-*.mjs and native-host-hooks.js. Rebuild with python tools/build_native.py; never patch generated root entries, bundles, worker, data, CSS or copied real-sky/core. vendor/real-sky retains immutable scientific source and oracle fixtures. The requested bottom-border fix is authored in tools/native_core_horizon.py; the builder applies that one digest-guarded horizon-predicate correction while copying the core. Keep its boundary and drift regression tests with the change. Run its builders/tests in a disposable copy. Historical PASS does not qualify this candidate. The existing gates below remain requirements, not blanket PASS.

The dependent Moon candidate adds authored moon/src/, lossless moon/assets/ and the supplied moon/moon_kernel.wasm. tools/build_moon.py runs through the native builder; never edit its generated host/worker/chunks or expanded entries. Native phase/time/configuration still belong to src/native/index.html; the device-resolution lunar foreground belongs to moon/src/moon-detail.mjs. Read docs/moon/QUALIFICATION.md for this candidate's evidence and limitations. The CP9 comparison ledger remains PARTIAL/BLOCKED; Moon integration does not close N001/N002/N003 or authorize merge/deployment.

Golden rules
Screenshots override metrics. A passing qaState() number does not pass a cycle if the screenshot looks wrong. Every visual claim needs a crop/clip.
Truthfulness over drama. Never make the widget claim a condition it can't support (see "Weather" below).
Do not commit unless explicitly asked. When asked, main is the GitHub Pages deploy branch.
No broad refactors mixed into a feature/fix. Keep diffs inspectable. Document before refactoring.
Physics gates the art. Optical phenomena must be condition-gated (ice vs droplet, low-sun + broken cloud, humidity, etc.), never random or always-on.
Subagent roles & what each reviews
GitHub/source auditor — confirms the committed index.html matches what's served; lists the relevant systems before any edit.
Runtime DOM/CSS/canvas auditor — measures live geometry (header/footer, cloud band vs dashed horizon, moon layers/radius/alpha + disc opacity/occlusion (no stars through), buckle cut-out vs strap, rain origin vs cloud columns) and reports numbers + crops.
Live-motion auditor — proves the default real-time widget actually animates over 15–60s (cloud drift/morph, star scintillation, sky breathing) via &debugMotion=1 Δ / a clip / a centroid-drift probe. Must NOT cite the qaState().clouds.hash as motion evidence (it flips on sub-pixel change — it produced false PASS reports).
Atmospheric-optics researcher — supplies condition gates, geometry, colour orders, gradient recipes for each phenomenon before it is coded.
Islamic dawn / Fajr semantics researcher — verifies false-dawn (vertical) vs true-dawn (horizontal) and the Fajr depression range; confirms dawn visuals never drive the prayer clock.
Solar / lunar renderer art directors — judge sun placement/optics and moon PBR/earthshine/halo/corona from forced-condition crops.
Cloud/weather lighting judge — structure, lighting, weather linkage, and continuity (no slideshow).
Star/night-sky judge — variety, twinkle (visible but not cartoonish), moon wash, location/weather response.
UI/layout invariant judge — footer visible + header geometry + readability in every scene.
Documentation architect / code-comment reviewer — keep DESIGN.md/AGENTS.md and the high-value comments true.
Skeptic visual panel (≥5) — may FAIL any cycle; must list failures and residual approximations.
Regression judge — diffs old screenshots vs current; flags anything that got worse.

Note: judges that drive the live preview must run sequentially (one shared preview server; parallel judges stomp on each other's scenes). State this honestly rather than faking a simultaneous panel.

Required PASS/FAIL gates

A cycle PASSES only when, with screenshot/clip evidence:

A — Sun is a defined radiant body with a clear nucleus, not a vague brush; colour is tone-mapped/white- balanced (airmass + transmittance + CCT + ACES) — under cloud it goes warm-white, never a grey/purple blob.
B — Sunrise enters low from the left near the horizon (warm glowing disc); sunset sky is warm (not generic daylight); low-sun colour believable; low-sun refraction flattening.
C — Solar optics distinct + gated (halo / parhelia / pillar / crepuscular / anticrepuscular / refraction), each only under its physical condition, and registered to the VISIBLE corner sun (--sunvx/--sunvy) — a center- screen halo is a FAIL.
D — Moon is OPAQUE every night (no stars through the disc) and meaningfully present every night — a new/ below-horizon moon shows a faint ashen opaque calendar disc with NO moonlight (never blank, never faked light); the disc is mostly in frame so the phase reads. Earthshine correct across crescent/half/gibbous/full (gibbous dark side faint but textured, never a black cutout).
E — Lunar corona (small, close) vs 22° halo (large ring) vs paraselenae (lateral, rare) are distinct + gated.
F — Dawn is honest, not painted: true dawn is the real physical twilight sky (dark at Fajr depth, brightening toward sunrise) + the Fajr marker — no horizontal "true-dawn band." False dawn is fail-closed (not rendered) — no diagonal cone / lens-flare slash, and nothing under a bright moon.
G — Clouds structured, lit, weather-linked; small distinct cells; mostly around/above the dashed 0° horizon.
H — Rain/lightning originate from cloud systems and vary by weather type/intensity.
I — Stars beautiful/alive/varied; not a spinning or static image; anchors + their glints scintillate.
J — Header belt (buckle cut-out, no strap through it) + footer + prayer UI intact and readable in every scene.
M0 (live motion) — the default real-time widget VISIBLY animates over 15–60s where the scene allows (clouds drift/morph, stars scintillate, sky breathes). Proven by a real watch / &debugMotion=1 Δ, NEVER the qaState hash. Accessibility: prefers-reduced-motion reduces it by default; &motion=full overrides.
K/L/M — DESIGN.md + AGENTS.md + HANDOFF.md current; high-value comments present; approximations stated honestly.
Evidence requirements (per cycle)

Crops/clips for: clear-day apex (defined nucleus), sunrise (enters low-left), sunset (warm sky), overcast (warm-white sun, not grey/purple), forced parhelia/halo/pillar (ringing the visible sun), forced crepuscular/anticrepuscular, crescent (right limb in frame)/half/gibbous/full moon, new moon (opaque ashen calendar disc), moon-opacity proof (no stars through the disc), forced lunar corona/halo/paraselene, daytime clouds, moonlit night clouds, rain + thunder, star twinkle, header buckle cut-out (zoom — no strap through), header/footer, near-Fajr (real twilight, no painted dawn band/cone). Plus a real 15–60s live-motion clip / debugMotion 10s–60s Δ (the headline gate), 5m/15m/60m/day simulated deltas, and motion=full vs reduced-motion. Judges list failures and residual approximations. Screenshots/Δ — never the qaState hash — decide motion.

Forbidden regressions (instant FAIL)
No visible motion in normal live real-time view (a static "wallpaper" sky). Verify with a real 15–60s watch / &debugMotion=1 10s–60s Δ — NOT the qaState().clouds.hash (it flips on sub-pixel change and lies).
The moon rendered transparent — stars visible through the disc, in ANY phase. The Moon is an opaque body.
An empty moon slot / moonless normal night. A new/below-horizon moon must still show a faint ashen OPAQUE calendar disc (no moonlight) — never blank sky, never a "new moon invisible" rule.
A painted false-dawn cone or horizontal true-dawn band/strip. Dawn = the real physical twilight sky + the Fajr marker; false dawn is fail-closed (not rendered) until properly modeled.
The sun rendered as a dim grey/purple blob or a vague brush with no defined nucleus (use the scene- referred tone-map; cloud → warm-white, never cold grey).
Solar optics (halo / sundogs / pillar) detached from the visible sun (they must register to --sunvx/--sunvy, not the arc-sun azimuth). A center-screen halo is an instant FAIL.
Footer date row clipped or any header change that moves the content stack.
Builder/embed: the iframe wrapper size drifting from the widget card — it must be 325×530 (= .c) in the builder preview, the copy snippet, README, and the TablissNG preset (an oversized wrapper adds invisible margin and misaligns the builder card/buttons).
Header buckle off-centre, straps full-width, a heavy drop shadow, or any strap geometry visible THROUGH the translucent buckle (the strap inner ends must be masked/cut, not merely z-indexed — translucent glass reveals what's under it).
Sunrise marker drawn as a filled dot (it is a ring) or off the dashed line; Maghrib off the line; Dhuhr on the apex.
The moon's dark limb rendered as a black cutout, or a jaggy/stroked moon edge.
A generic glow standing in for a gated optical phenomenon.
Claiming direct local rain/lightning observations from model or uncalibrated radar data, or letting hourly forecasts overwrite current conditions in real time. The owner's PR42 policy explicitly permits labelled fresh current-model rain/snow with supporting admitted quantities. Keep condition presentation, model effect permissions and direct-observation authority separate; see DESIGN.md.
Clouds that reseed / slideshow on weather refresh or per render tick.
Replacing the accurate PBR moon lighting with a flat sprite; making physics "ugly".
Commit policy

Do not commit or push unless the user explicitly asks. When asked: commit the relevant source + docs (index.html, config.js, builder.html, install.sh/install.ps1, presets/, tests/, the *.md docs) — never the stray research scratch files (noaa_clouds.html, *_photopills.html, _mag_extract.txt, etc.). main deploys to GitHub Pages, so a commit to main is a deploy. End commit messages with the standard Co-Authored-By line.

Running / debugging common scenarios

Configuration and diagnostics are read from the fragment after #. Append &debugMotion=1 or &motion=full to that same fragment. A query-only ?debugMotion=1 is not read. The six debugOptic force names are halo, sundogs, pillar, anticrep, paraselene and lunarhalo. Corona, earthshine, refraction and the crepuscular ray require controlled physical scene inputs; no dedicated debugOptic switch forces them.

Real-time motion diagnostic:

index.html#lat=24.47&lon=39.61&label=Madinah&method=4&debugMotion=1


Full-motion override (the normal default respects reduced motion):

index.html#lat=24.47&lon=39.61&label=Madinah&method=4&debugMotion=1&motion=full


Solar noon halo diagnostic:

index.html#lat=24.47&lon=39.61&label=Madinah&method=4&simTime=12:30&debugOptic=halo


Query-only negative control: these flags are not read from before #.

index.html?debugMotion=1&motion=full#lat=24.47&lon=39.61


simTime without timeScale freezes the clock-driven scene. Use the real-time recipe above for a 15–60 second motion check. Flag activation alone does not prove visible motion or correct optical pixels.

Lunar force checks require an eligible night Moon. Near-new, below-horizon, daylight and unavailable-surface cases cannot gain moonlight from a diagnostic flag. Retain the physical scene inputs and crops for optics, and the real 15–60 second watch/clip/delta for motion; never use qaState().clouds.hash as motion proof.

Serve the folder statically and open index.html#lat=24.47&lon=39.61&label=Madinah&method=4.

Day positions: &simTime=12:30 (noon), &simTime=05:50 (sunrise), &simTime=18:55 (sunset/golden hour).
Weather visuals: &simWx=2&simCloud=50 (broken), &simWx=3&simCloud=100 (overcast), &simWx=63 (rain), &simWx=95 (thunder), &simWx=45 (fog).
Weather-truth QA: &simWx=95&simPrecip=0 must downgrade (no thunder/rain); &simWx=95&simPrecip=5 keeps thunder; check qaState().wxTruth for the source/reason chain.
Moon: &simMoon=0.08&simWax=1&simMoonAlt=20&simMoonH=42 (crescent), &simMoon=0.92… (gibbous), &simMoon=0.98… (full); thin-cloud halo/corona via &simWx=2&simCloud=30 on a moon scene.
Live motion: load real-time (no simTime) and watch ~15–60s — clouds must drift/morph, stars scintillate, sky breathe. &debugMotion=1 shows rAF/s, cloud-paint/s, reduced-motion, paused, cloud Δ 10s/60s, star Δ, reason. &motion=full forces motion under OS reduced-motion. &timeScale=1800 fast-forwards a day.
Moon opacity: any night moon — confirm no stars show through the disc; new moon (&simMoon=0.01) shows a faint opaque ashen calendar disc with qaState().moonTruth.moonlightOpacity == 0.
Readouts: &debugLayers=1, &debugMoon=1, &debugMotion=1, &qa=1 then window.qaState() (incl. wxTruth, moonTruth). &debugDawn=… is a deprecated no-op (dawn is not painted).
Preview gotcha: simTime without timeScale freezes the clock (TIMESCALE 0), so cloud drift won't be visible in a still test — use the direct paintClouds(t) probe or a real-time / timeScale watch to see motion.
Frozen V1 compatibility snapshot

v1/ is the frozen pre-overhaul compatibility snapshot. Normal builds and renderer integrations must neither regenerate, overwrite nor delete it. Any deliberate change requires explicit owner authority and disclosure.

Run python tools/verify_v1.py after builds/integrations. It verifies V1 independently of the current root runtime. See docs/V1_PRESERVATION.md for provenance, storage isolation, focused comparison checks and the pending deployment smoke procedure.
